verdict_reason: The HEADLINE statistic is exact and correctly null-calibrated: on 50 randomised causal attention heads BLME's per-row Spearman matches a hand-written tie-averaged rank correlation to 6.245e-17, and on an exactly uniform causal pattern -- where by construction there is no positional decay -- it returns EXACTLY 0.000000000000 at L = 4, 8, 64 and 256. I CONFIRM codex's pooled-companion defect and add the quantification that makes it minor: the key named for the manuscript's equation, mean_positional_decay_correlation_pooled, starts its loop at query 1 and so omits the (0,0) pair despite the comment above it claiming 'EVERY causal {i, j} pair ... diagonal included'. On uniform L=4 that is -0.365881926131 against the true all-pair -0.476666666667, but the gap collapses with context (-0.469444 vs -0.434477 at L=8; -0.466670 vs -0.466622 at L=256, i.e. 4.8e-5) and the largest gap over 50 random heads is 0.065554. The far bigger issue with that same key is not the missing pair: the pooled statistic reads -0.466621537069 on its OWN NULL at L=256, which the file documents and which is why it is not the headline.
comparable_reason: The headline is an unweighted mean over every (layer, head, query row), and the per-layer profile is strongly non-flat, so depth alone moves it. Measured on gpt2 (5 passages, fp32, eager attention): layer means run -0.2740, -0.3578, -0.4885, -0.5236, -0.4876, -0.3215, -0.3954, -0.2767, -0.2935, -0.1278, -0.0971, +0.0027 -- the last layer is at the null. A model with proportionally more late-style layers reads closer to 0 for architectural reasons, and the arithmetic is explicit: appending k layers at the null moves a mean of v over n layers to v*n/(n+k). The raw number is also contaminated by the attention sink, whose mass I measured at 0.469173422 on gpt2 -- position 0 is simultaneously the largest-mass key and the maximum-distance key in every causal row -- and the file cites 14.5% on pythia-70m, a 3.2x spread that does not cancel across models.
github_reason: No code was released for this metric, because it is not a published metric: RoFormer (Su et al. 2021) and ALiBi (Press et al. 2021) motivate the long-range-decay PREMISE but define no attention-distance Spearman diagnostic, and task_metadata.py:64 correctly lists no upstream repository and labels the task 'proxy-only'. I verified the estimator against an independent hand-written tie-averaged rank correlation instead (6.245e-17) and against the analytic uniform-causal null (exactly 0.0 at four context lengths).
paper_reason: Neither motivating paper publishes a scalar this diagnostic should reproduce (RoFormer's Table 2 is an STS-B score). The BLME manuscript (sections/metrics_geometry.tex:246-251) does publish a defining EQUATION, and the code's own comments record that the shipped headline is not that equation -- the manuscript's pooled form is emitted under a separate key at -0.507450034 on gpt2 while the headline reads -0.303397847, a 67% difference in the same output dict. The reconciliation is tracked in RERUN_LEDGER.md but is not done.
confounds_reason: Two measured mechanisms, both architectural rather than behavioural. (1) DEPTH: the gpt2 per-layer profile spans -0.5236 to +0.0027, so the layer-averaged headline is a function of how many layers a model has and where its decay peak sits, independent of any positional-encoding property. (2) SINK: sink mass is 0.469173422 on gpt2 against the file's measured 0.145 on pythia-70m, and because the sink sits at the maximum-distance end of every causal row, that 3.2x spread enters the correlation directly -- gpt2's raw -0.303397847 becomes -0.424593205 with the sink removed, a shift of 0.121. The sink-excluded twin is correctly demoted to _meta_ rather than being sold as the fix.
defects: CODE / COMMENT CONTRADICTS CODE IN THE MANUSCRIPT-MATCHING KEY (positional_decay.py:191-196). The comment says the pooled branch takes 'EVERY causal {i, j} pair, exactly as the manuscript writes it -- diagonal included, and from q = 1'; the loop `for _q in range(1, seq_len)` therefore omits (0,0). Effect: -0.365881926131 vs -0.476666666667 on uniform L=4, max 0.065554 over 50 random heads, and under 5e-5 at L=256. Either include q=0 or change the comment; the code as written is neither the manuscript's set nor a documented restriction.

CODE / THE TWO EMITTED VARIANTS USE DIFFERENT PAIR SETS. The rowwise headline reads `a[head, q, :q]` -- the DIAGONAL (distance 0) is excluded -- while the pooled branch reads `a[head, q, :q+1]` and includes it. Both are internally consistent but the difference is undocumented, so the two keys are not two aggregations of one pair set.

COMPARABILITY (not an implementation defect): headline = unweighted mean over a layer profile spanning -0.5236..+0.0027 on gpt2, so it tracks depth; and it carries a 46.9% sink mass on gpt2 vs 14.5% on pythia-70m.

PROTOCOL / CONFIG (not an implementation defect): defaults.yaml gives num_samples=5 with a study override of 50, and the context is capped at 256 tokens in code. task_metadata.py:64 describes this as a 'long-context-only aggregate decay trend', which 256 tokens does not operationalise -- and since the pooled companion's null bias itself converges only as L grows (-0.434 at L=8 vs -0.467 at L=256), the context cap interacts with the statistic.

GOOD PRACTICE WORTH KEEPING: _row_distance_correlation returns the null ONLY for an exactly flat row (ptp == 0.0, not <= 1e-12), the attention tensor is promoted to fp32 before any rank comparison, and _meta_n_flat_attn_rows / _meta_n_nonfinite_attn_rows / _meta_model_dtype are emitted so a dtype-driven number is detectable from the output. All three were real bugs and all three fixes check out.
